audit.title: Chainlink Functions Service Responsibility

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Working — opens with "Chainlink Functions provides access to trust-minimized compute infrastructure…" and each section leads with a plain statement of who is responsible. Weak — no single liftable sentence defines the "shared responsibility model" itself as a concept.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Working — 7 headings, 1 H1, max depth H3, 0 level skips, no section over 240 words (measured). Weak — the developer-vs-node-operator split is ideal for a comparison table; 0 tables present.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Weak — 0 numerals, 0 units (measured), and vague quantifiers ("several," "when possible," "timely manner"). No limits, expiration defaults, or DON node counts that would anchor an extractable fact.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Weak — 1 internal link (to llms.txt), 0 external, 0 primary sources (measured). Claims about secrets, subscriptions, DONs, and OCR consensus link to nothing.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Working — the trust-minimized-compute sentence is liftable. Weak — "service responsibility" / shared-responsibility model lacks a crisp one-line definition near first use.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak — 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, datePublished/dateModified absent (measured). Head metadata was not captured, so this could not be fully verified from the served `<head>`; CLI should pass raw `<head>` for a complete read.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Not applicable — this is a policy/conceptual page; no code is expected and none is missing. Not penalized.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Working — covers "developer responsibilities" and "node operator responsibilities." Weak — no "who is responsible for X" question phrasing, no FAQ, no coverage of the service shutdown implications a reader would now ask about.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; consistent "Chainlink Functions" naming throughout, unambiguous prose. No action needed.

audit.summary: This is a cleanly written conceptual page defining the shared-responsibility split between developers and node operators for Chainlink Functions. Its biggest strength is clean, consistent prose with a sensible H2/H3 hierarchy; its biggest opportunity is the total absence of a comparison table, citations, and machine-readable metadata — all high-lift GEO factors for a page whose core content (a two-party responsibility split) is table-shaped. Note also that the page carries a `callout="shutdown"` flag, meaning the underlying service is being deprecated: relevance and freshness signals matter more than deep polish here. Honest verdict: solid documentation, under-optimized for generative retrieval.

recommendations.title: Add a developer-vs-node-operator responsibility table
recommendations.where: top of page, after the intro paragraph
recommendations.issue: the split is spread across ~720 words of prose with 0 tables (measured).
recommendations.change: add a 2-column table (Responsibility area | Developer / Node Operator owner) summarizing Data, Code, Secrets, Subscriptions, Node config, Consensus. Put the canonical owner in the first cell of each row.
recommendations.why: tables are directly extractable by engines building a "who owns what" answer; a lifted row stands alone.

recommendations.title: Add question-phrased H3s
recommendations.change: reframe or add subheads like "Who is responsible for funding a Functions subscription?" and "Who secures self-hosted secrets?"
recommendations.why: devs query by question, not by concept noun; question headings win retrieval that label headings lose.

recommendations.title: Add inline citations to canonical docs
recommendations.issue: 0 external/primary links (measured); concepts are named but unlinked.
recommendations.change: link each term to its canonical Chainlink docs page (secrets management, subscriptions, DON architecture) and OCR to its spec.
recommendations.why: inline links to primary sources raise credibility and citation rate.

recommendations.title: Add a crisp shared-responsibility definition
recommendations.issue: "both developers and Chainlink service providers share responsibility" is diffuse.
recommendations.change: add one liftable sentence, e.g. "Under the Chainlink Functions shared-responsibility model, developers own data quality, code, secrets, and subscription funding, while node operators own DON configuration, execution, and consensus uptime."
recommendations.why: a self-contained canonical statement is preferred for verbatim lifting.

recommendations.title: Add TechArticle JSON-LD, canonical URL, and last-updated
recommendations.change: emit `TechArticle` schema with `dateModified`, a canonical URL, and a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: structured metadata and freshness signals improve agent trust and parseability (E-E-A-T).

recommendations.title: Replace vague quantifiers with specifics where they exist
recommendations.where: node operator bullets and secrets section
recommendations.change: where a concrete value exists (e.g. secret expiration defaults, minimum node count in a DON, funding thresholds), state the number; otherwise link to the page that has it.
recommendations.why: quantitative claims are among the highest-lift retrievable elements.

recommendations.title: Surface the service-shutdown status prominently in prose
recommendations.where: intro, currently only a `<ChainlinkFunctions callout="shutdown" />` component
recommendations.issue: shutdown status is component-rendered and may not survive text extraction.
recommendations.change: add a plain-text sentence stating the service status and effective date so it is liftable by engines that skip the component.
recommendations.why: deprecation status is the highest-value fact a reader now needs; component-only rendering risks it being invisible to extractors.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifiers: "several," "when possible," "timely manner," "latest software versions" (measured: vague quantifier "several" present).
No dated/freshness signal on a page describing a service in shutdown — stale-risk for generative answers.
Component-embedded shutdown notice (`<ChainlinkFunctions callout="shutdown" />`) may not extract as text.
No keyword stuffing, no marketing fluff, no unresolved cross-references — clean on those.
offPageNotes: Site-level: `llms.txt` is already referenced (good); ensure this page is indexed there and in the sitemap.
Head metadata (schema, canonical, dates) could not be verified from the served content — pass raw `<head>` in the CLI for a definitive read.
Freshness cadence: given the shutdown state, a site-wide dateModified policy would materially help engines avoid presenting deprecated guidance as current.
